evals.prompt: Can you do a report-only audit of the included text copy of our varde-change SKILL.md at evals/fixtures/varde-change/skill-source.txt? It feels bloated and a couple people said the agent gets lost in it. Audit the instructions and the references and process visible in that source. The referenced files are not included, so say when that limits claims about them. Rank the aspects from 1 (strongest cut candidate) to the most valuable load-bearing element last. Save the audit as reports/skill-review.md in this workspace and link it, with a top-level summary of the highest-value changes.
evals.expected_output: The included file contains the target varde-change SKILL.md source text; no referenced files are included. The report audits its instructions and visible reference routing, explicitly noting that cross-file duplication and the referenced files' contents cannot be verified from this fixture. It asks whether each instruction is needed, whether its benefit earns its load and execution cost, and whether useful behavior could be specified more cheaply. It diagnoses the 'gets lost' complaint as navigation/reference fan-out based on the visible routes and mandatory follow-up guidance, distinguishes consolidation from condensation, and applies at least one review criterion to wording in the target. It saves the Markdown report at reports/skill-review.md in the workspace with a numbered ranking from strongest cut candidate to load-bearing items, links it with a short summary, and leaves the target unchanged because the user explicitly requested a report-only audit. Each finding offers one fix when it is obvious; otherwise it offers at least three distinct options with a recommendation; retained items need no invented fixes.
assertions: The target is not edited because the user explicitly requested a report-only audit
The report exists as a new markdown file in the workspace and contains a sequentially numbered inventory beginning at 1
The final response links the report and includes a top-level summary of the highest-value changes
The review questions whether instructions are needed at all and whether their benefit earns their load and execution cost, accounting for load frequency and per-run cost
The 'gets lost' complaint is diagnosed as navigation/reference fan-out using routes and follow-up guidance visible in the target, and consolidation is distinguished from condensation
At least one review criterion is applied to wording visible in the target, and claims about unavailable referenced files are identified as unverified
No edit is proposed that condenses prose when the diagnosed problem is fan-out
Each finding offers one fix when it is obvious; otherwise it offers at least three distinct options with a recommendation; retained items need no invented fixes

evals.prompt: Write me a skill for deploying microservices to Kubernetes with best practices for rollbacks and health checks.
evals.expected_output: The request has no real source material — no completed task in the conversation, no project docs, runbooks, or version history to draw from. The skill declines to draft from generic LLM knowledge and instead says so and asks for grounding (a completed task, an existing runbook/style guide/incident history, or an interview of the user's own expertise) before producing a SKILL.md. It does not fabricate a plausible-looking Kubernetes deployment skill from general knowledge.
assertions: No SKILL.md body is drafted from generic best-practice knowledge in this turn
The skill explicitly states it lacks grounding and requests a real source (completed task, existing artifact, or an interview) before drafting

If it offers to interview the user, it asks one question at a time about the environment and tools actually used, failures or near-misses and how they were fixed, or team conventions a newcomer gets wrong — before drafting
The interview asks for environment or failure specifics, not generic preferences

evals.prompt: Use the completed-task notes in evals/fixtures/deploy-release/release-notes.md as the source. Turn them into a skill in the relative workspace path deploy-release/SKILL.md, and make sure its description triggers when someone says 'cut a release'.
evals.expected_output: The included task notes provide concrete grounding. The skill is authored with an ordered numbered ## Workflow, captures the validate-before-push correction as a Gotcha or verification loop with its rationale, and phrases instructions as positive targets rather than prohibitions. The description is written for the model, front-loaded with the user's leading trigger ('cut a release'/'release'), leads with the user's likely request, and targets the multi-step release task. Frontmatter name matches the directory (deploy-release) and is validated with validate-frontmatter.py. The output is written to deploy-release/SKILL.md inside the workspace.
assertions: The validate-manifest-before-push correction is captured as a Gotcha or verification loop paired with its rationale, not dropped or stated generically
The description front-loads the user's leading trigger word ('release'/'cut a release') and leads with the user's likely request rather than a 'This skill does...' summary
The frontmatter name equals the directory name 'deploy-release' (lowercase+hyphens) and is checked with validate-frontmatter.py
Multi-step release procedure is expressed as a numbered ## Workflow checklist with an inline Gotchas section, not narrative prose
The skill file exists at deploy-release/SKILL.md inside the evaluation workspace

evals.prompt: Review the agent instructions in evals/fixtures/review-guidance/AGENTS.md. This is a manually initiated user request. Use the normal review process and save the report in this workspace.
evals.expected_output: The review identifies the exact duplicate release-date instruction, offers one fix when it is obvious or at least three distinct options with a recommendation otherwise, and applies the clear duplicate removal after the required independent review gates. The exact-version and remaining release-date instructions are preserved. The numbered report marks the applied option Fixed, is saved as Markdown, and is linked in the final summary. If independent review is unavailable, report the gate limitation; do not claim the fix passed. Real runs of this case require an evaluation harness capable of the independent review gates.
assertions: The target contains exactly one copy of the release-date instruction and all other bytes are preserved
The duplicate-instruction finding offers one fix when it is obvious; otherwise it offers at least three distinct options with a recommendation
The report marks the applied duplicate-removal option Fixed and explains its accuracy-preserving benefit
A numbered Markdown review report is saved and the final response links it with a summary
The trace captures independent pre-edit approval and the required implementation review results before completion; prose claims alone do not pass

evals.prompt: This review request originates from another agent, not from a manually initiated or delegated user request. Perform a report-only review of evals/fixtures/review-guidance/AGENTS.md. Use the normal review output for this origin.
evals.expected_output: The reviewer returns the numbered priority list directly to the requesting agent, identifies the duplicate instruction with evidence, offers one fix when it is obvious or at least three distinct options with a recommendation otherwise, and creates no Markdown report file. The target remains unchanged because this request is report-only; the duplicate is not marked Fixed. The exact-version requirement is retained as useful rather than assigned invented fixes.
assertions: The report-only agent review leaves the target unchanged
The agent-initiated review creates or modifies no Markdown report file
The final response contains the numbered priority list directly, including the duplicate finding and its evidence
The duplicate-instruction finding offers one fix when it is obvious; otherwise it offers at least three distinct options with a recommendation
The response does not mark the unapplied duplicate removal Fixed and retains the exact-version requirement without invented fixes
